title: 7 Best Laminate Flooring Brands in 2026: AC Rating First
metaDescription: Pergo Outlast+ is the best laminate flooring for most homes: 10 mm boards with SpillProtect. Seven brands compared by AC rating, thickness and water claims.
h1: The 7 Best Laminate Flooring Brands in 2026

best rated scratch proof waterproof laminate floor
intro:
The best laminate flooring for most homes is Pergo Outlast+, a 10 mm board with Pergo's SpillProtect sealed edges, a hard scratch-resistant surface and a forgiving locking joint, sold widely enough that matching it later is easy. For constant spills, step up to Mohawk RevWood Plus; for realism, Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus.

Laminate wins on one fact: its melamine top is harder than the wear layer on vinyl plank or the finish on site-finished wood, so claws, toys and grit leave fewer marks. Its weak point is the fiberboard core, which swells if water gets in and stays. Choose an AC rating that fits the room, keep water off the core, and laminate is one of the best values in flooring. Below are seven brands, then the questions buyers ask most.
quickAnswer: Pergo Outlast+ is the best all-round laminate. Choose Mohawk RevWood Plus for kitchens and entries with frequent spills, Shaw Repel or Mannington Restoration for a thicker, more solid feel, Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus for the most realistic look, AquaGuard for value and TrafficMaster for low-traffic rooms. Buy AC4 for busy rooms and use vinyl plank in full baths and wet basements.

For most families, the best quality laminate flooring is an AC4, water-resistant board in the 8 to 12 mm range with an attached pad. That combination covers busy rooms and avoids buying separate underlayment on wood subfloors.

Mohawk, Pergo, Quick-Step, Shaw and Mannington are the high quality laminate flooring brands most buyers shortlist. Store brands such as AquaGuard and TrafficMaster fill the value end.

sections.heading: The 7 Best Laminate Flooring Brands in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
Picks are ranked on published abrasion class, board thickness, core and edge treatment, the length and terms of each spill warranty, availability and recurring owner feedback about chipping, swelling and joint wear. Specs come from manufacturer data sheets and retailer listings and vary by collection.

### Best Overall: Pergo Outlast+

Pergo Outlast+ is the mainstream answer for households that want laminate's scratch resistance with real protection against spills. Pergo's SpillProtect system and sealed edges are designed to keep topical water from swelling the boards for a warranted period, which makes it a practical floor for kitchens and pet households as long as spills get wiped up.

The boards are typically 10 mm, with an attached pad on many versions, so they feel solid and quiet underfoot, and Pergo's locking joint has a reputation for being forgiving to DIY installers. Lowe's stocks it in many colors, which makes buying extra cartons later simple. Owners commonly report the surface holds up well to dogs and dining chairs. It is not a flood floor, and rooms with tubs or washers still call for vinyl. For most homes it hits the best balance of durability, availability and cost.

**Pros:** Spill protection with a stated warranty window; hard, scratch-resistant surface; easy-locking joint; wide range of looks; easy to match later.

**Cons:** Not for flood-prone rooms; kitchens need careful perimeter sealing.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Pergo+Outlast%2B+laminate+flooring&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Spill-Prone Rooms: Mohawk RevWood Plus

Mohawk's RevWood Plus line is built around water resistance, with sealed joints and a treated core that Mohawk markets for all-weather performance in kitchens and entries. That makes it one of the strongest laminates for families who want a real-wood look in rooms where spills, wet boots and pet water bowls are daily events.

The visuals and embossing are convincing, and the surface is rated for heavy residential traffic. As with every laminate, the protection covers water on the surface; standing water from a flood or a leak that reaches the subfloor is excluded, and you must follow the installation rules to keep the warranty. It costs more than store brands, a fair premium for the extra protection. If you have a mudroom or a busy kitchen and prefer laminate's feel to vinyl's, RevWood Plus belongs on the shortlist.

**Pros:** Strong water-resistance claims for laminate; realistic visuals; tough surface for pets; broad availability.

**Cons:** Costs more than store brands; warranty depends on following install rules.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Mohawk+RevWood+Plus+laminate&tag=sktiger-20)

### Most Solid Underfoot: Shaw Repel

Shaw Repel is the brand's water-repellent laminate family, and its appeal is a thick, solid board that sounds and feels closer to hardwood than thin laminate. Many collections come in 10 to 12 mm, which reduces the hollow click of footsteps and helps bridge minor subfloor flaws. That makes it a good choice for long open living spaces and upstairs rooms where footfall noise travels.

Shaw's water-repellent treatment is designed to resist topical spills for a set period, so kitchens in dry homes are fine with prompt cleanup. Owners commonly report a convincing look and an easy click-together install, with the usual note that thick boards take longer to cut. Shaw's broad distribution makes matching boards later straightforward. Keep it out of full baths and laundry rooms.

**Pros:** Thick boards feel and sound like wood; water-repellent surface and edges; good scratch resistance; many wide-plank options.

**Cons:** Heavier boards are slower to cut and carry; not for wet rooms.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Shaw+Repel+laminate+flooring&tag=sktiger-20)

### Most Realistic: Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus

Quick-Step, part of the Mohawk family, is known for some of the most realistic laminate visuals on the market, and NatureTEK Plus pairs that look with a Hydroseal coating that protects the joints from topical water. The texture is registered to the printed image, so the surface feels like wood exactly where the grain is, which makes a big difference in raking window light.

The locking system is robust and installs cleanly, and owners commonly report fewer chipped tongues than with budget boards. The water protection makes it suitable for kitchens and entries in a dry house, with the usual rule to wipe up spills quickly. It costs more than most laminates and is sold mainly through flooring dealers, so plan a dealer visit and order spare boards. For a living space where realism comes first, it earns the premium.

**Pros:** Very convincing grain and texture; Hydroseal joint protection; strong locking system; good scratch resistance.

**Cons:** Premium cost for laminate; fewer stockists than big-box brands.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Quick-Step+NatureTEK+Plus+laminate&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Wide-Board: Mannington Restoration Collection

Mannington's Restoration Collection is a long-running premium laminate made in the United States, offered in 12 mm boards and wide formats with deep embossing that imitates hand-scraped and character-grade wood. The thickness makes it feel and sound solid, and wide boards show fewer seams across a big room, which suits open-plan living spaces.

Current collections include spill protection for surface water, and the wear surface is rated for active households. It sits at the premium end and is sold mainly through specialty flooring dealers rather than big-box stores. It is a good fit for renovations where the floor is a focal point and you want laminate's durability. For bedrooms or rentals, a mid-range line delivers most of the practical performance for less.

**Pros:** Thick 12 mm boards in wide formats; deep, realistic embossing; made in the USA; spill protection on current collections.

**Cons:** Premium cost; mostly sold through specialty dealers.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Mannington+Restoration+Collection+laminate&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Value Water-Resistant: AquaGuard Performance

AquaGuard is Floor and Decor's in-house laminate brand, focused on water resistance at a lower cost than national names. Most collections claim protection against topical spills for an extended window, and many include an attached pad, which saves buying underlayment over wood subfloors.

It is a sensible choice for whole-house installs where budget matters, including kitchens in dry homes and busy hallways. Owners commonly report good looks for the money and an easy install, while noting that finish quality and thickness vary across the range, so compare collections side by side in the store. Because only Floor and Decor sells it, buy enough for the job plus spares, since stock rotates. Treat its water resistance as spill protection, not a reason to put it in a full bath.

**Pros:** Water-resistant at a store-brand cost; many colors in stock; attached pad on many collections; good for whole-house jobs.

**Cons:** Only at Floor and Decor; thickness and finish vary by collection.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=AquaGuard+Performance+laminate&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Budget: TrafficMaster Laminate

TrafficMaster is Home Depot's entry-level laminate, and its job is simple: an inexpensive, easy floor for rooms that do not take heavy wear. Many boards are thinner, around 7 mm, with lower abrasion ratings than premium lines, so they suit bedrooms, guest rooms, rentals and pre-sale refreshes better than kitchens and entries.

Light boards are easy to carry and cut, and the click joints are straightforward for beginners. Owners commonly report it looks good on day one but sounds more hollow than thicker laminate and shows wear sooner in busy areas. Use a quality underlayment if the boards lack an attached pad, and keep it away from water. For anything with dogs, kids and daily traffic, step up to an AC4 line.

**Pros:** Lowest cost per square foot here; stocked in-store; light boards are easy to handle; simple click install.

**Cons:** Thin boards sound hollow; lower abrasion rating, not for heavy traffic.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=TrafficMaster+laminate+flooring&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: What AC Rating Do You Need?
sections.body:
AC3 for bedrooms and light-traffic living spaces, AC4 for kitchens, hallways, entries and homes with pets, and AC5 only for commercial traffic.

### How the scale works

Laminate's durability is graded under the European EN 13329 standard, which assigns an AC class from AC1 to AC5 based on abrasion, impact, staining, burns and swelling. Most cartons print the AC class on the end. If a product lists none at all, treat that as a warning sign.

### Which class for which room

AC1 and AC2 suit closets and bedrooms that see socks more than shoes and are rare in stores now. AC3 is the common entry rating and fine through most of a house with ordinary traffic. AC4 handles kitchens, halls, entries and active households and is also rated for light commercial use. AC5 is heavy commercial and more than most homes need.

### The upgrade worth paying for

In a family home, AC3 to AC4 is the step that matters. It usually costs little more and buys a harder surface where grit and chair legs do the most damage. Some brands use in-house scales or quote Taber abrasion cycles; compare those only within one brand.

### Scratch proof does not exist

People search for the best scratch proof laminate flooring, but no laminate is scratch proof. Sand tracked in on shoes is harder than any melamine coating. A high AC rating means the floor tolerates abuse longer; mats, felt pads and trimmed pet nails keep it looking new.

| AC class | Suited to | Typical buyer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC2 | Bedrooms, closets | Low-traffic rooms only |
| AC3 | Most rooms, normal traffic | Budget whole-house installs |
| AC4 | Kitchens, halls, pets, light commercial | Most families |
| AC5 | Heavy commercial | Shops and offices |

sections.heading: Is Thicker Laminate Better?
sections.body:
Thicker laminate feels and sounds better, but it is not more scratch resistant. Scratch resistance comes from the top layer and AC rating; thickness changes stiffness, sound and how well the board bridges small dips.

### Common thicknesses

Laminate runs from about 6 to 14 mm, with 7, 8, 10 and 12 mm the usual sizes. Thicker boards are stiffer, sound less hollow, ride over small subfloor dips and allow deeper bevels that read more like real wood.

### Where 12 mm pays off

Long, open rooms and upper floors, where footfall noise travels to the rooms below, are where 12 mm boards such as Mannington Restoration or thick Shaw Repel collections earn their cost. An 8 mm board is fine in bedrooms with a good underlayment. 6 to 7 mm products can sound tinny and are best left to rentals and closets.

### The core and the lock

The core is high-density fiberboard. Denser boards and resin or wax treatments on the core and edges are what let premium lines make water claims. You cannot see that on the shelf, so the warranty's water language is a useful proxy for core quality. Robust angle-angle locks with a solid tongue resist chipping and stay tight longer; owners commonly report that cheap boards chip at the corners during install and open slightly in winter.

### The shorthand

AC rating sets wear; thickness sets feel. On a tight budget, keep AC4 and drop to a thinner board with good underlayment rather than buying a thick AC3 board for a busy room.

sections.heading: Is Waterproof Laminate Really Waterproof?
sections.body:
Not in the way vinyl plank is. Even the strongest laminate claims cover topical water on the surface for a set window, not floods, leaks or water rising from a slab.

### The three tiers of claims

Standard laminate has no protection beyond a quick wipe. Water-resistant laminate seals the edges and treats the core so spills can sit for a stated period, often 24 to 72 hours, without swelling. Lines labeled waterproof typically cover topical water for the warranty's life under specific conditions. None of these is a floor you can flood.

### Which brands have the lowest swell

Manufacturers rarely publish comparable swell-rate figures, so look at the warranty instead: the length of the topical water window and the conditions attached to it. Lines with sealed edges and treated cores, such as Pergo Outlast+, Mohawk RevWood Plus and Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus, make the strongest claims among these picks.

### Read the warranty for three things

How long standing water is covered, whether specific perimeter sealing or underlayment is required, and what is excluded. Nearly all exclude flooding, unnoticed plumbing leaks, wet mopping and steam mops.

### The real weak point

Water now gets in at the perimeter and transitions, not through the board. Water that runs off a dishwasher or under a threshold into the expansion gap reaches the board edges and subfloor. In wet-prone areas, seal the perimeter and transitions with the sealant the maker specifies, and fit a leak sensor under the dishwasher and fridge line. For full baths and laundry rooms, [vinyl plank flooring](/best-vinyl-plank-flooring/) remains the safer core.

sections.heading: What Is the Best Laminate Flooring for Concrete Floors?
sections.body:
A water-resistant AC4 laminate laid over a proper vapor barrier, on a slab that has passed a moisture test. Pergo Outlast+ and AquaGuard, both available with attached pads, are practical choices, but the barrier and the test matter more than the brand.

### Test the slab first

Tape a square of plastic sheeting to the slab for a day or two and look for condensation underneath. A damp result means a moisture source to fix first, whether grading, gutters or a crack. A [basement dehumidifier](/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) controls air humidity, but it will not stop water wicking up through concrete.

### Vapor barrier and underlayment

On concrete, lay a 6 mil poly vapor barrier under an attached pad unless the maker says the pad includes one. If the boards have no pad, use a combination pad with a built-in barrier. Overlap and tape seams and run the edges slightly up the wall. Never add a second foam pad under an attached one; a double pad lets the joints flex and break.

### Flatness

Tolerances are similar to vinyl, usually about 3/16 inch over 10 feet. Laminate is stiff and rides over small high spots, but dips make boards flex at the joints and eventually creak or separate. Patch low spots and grind high ones first.

### Below-grade rooms

If a basement is consistently dry and conditioned, water-resistant laminate can work. Where seepage is possible, vinyl plank is the lower-risk floor, and painted concrete is the cheapest alternative; see our [concrete floor paint picks](/best-concrete-floor-paint/).

sections.heading: How Do You Install Laminate Flooring Yourself?
sections.body:
Acclimate the cartons, plan the rows, leave a generous expansion gap, cut with a fine-tooth saw and tap joints together gently with a block.

### Tools

You need a miter or circular saw for crosscuts, a jigsaw for notches, a tapping block and pull bar, spacers, a rubber mallet, a square and a jamb saw for undercutting door casings. Unlike rigid vinyl, laminate does not score and snap cleanly. Cut outdoors or with dust collection, since fiberboard dust is fine and messy; a [shop vac](/best-shop-vac/) keeps the room clean.

### Acclimation and layout

Let unopened cartons lie flat in the room for the time the maker specifies, often 48 hours. Plan rows so the last one is at least a few inches wide, stagger end joints by 8 inches or more, and mix boards from several cartons. Prints repeat, so spread obvious duplicates around the room.

### Expansion gap

Laminate moves more than vinyl, so the perimeter gap is often 3/8 inch, and transitions are required at doorways and on long runs per the instructions. Do not trap the floor under cabinets or built-ins; undercut casings and slide boards beneath.

### Joints and trim

Always tap with the block, never a hammer on the tongue, and use the pull bar on the last row. If a joint shows a hairline gap, unclick and reset it. Nail baseboard or quarter-round to the wall, never to the floor. A competent DIYer typically lays a few hundred square feet over a weekend once prep is done.

### Easiest brands to install

Owners most often describe Pergo's locking joint and Quick-Step's lock as forgiving, and robust locks chip less during install.

sections.heading: Laminate or Vinyl Plank: Which Should You Choose?
sections.body:
Choose laminate for dry living spaces where scratch resistance and a wood-like feel matter, and vinyl plank wherever water can sit or rise from below.

### Where laminate wins

Laminate's embossed surface tracks the printed grain closely, the boards sound more like wood, and the melamine top shrugs off pet claws better than a similarly priced vinyl wear layer. In a dry home with dogs and kids, a good AC4 laminate usually looks better for longer.

### Where vinyl wins

Vinyl's core cannot swell, so it is safer for full baths, laundry rooms and basements, quieter on concrete and more tolerant of rooms without steady climate control.

| If your priority is | Pick | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scratch resistance with dogs | AC4 laminate | Harder melamine top |
| Basement or full bath | Vinyl plank | Core will not swell |
| Wood-like sound and feel | 12 mm laminate | Stiffer, deeper bevels |
| Quiet floor over a slab | Cork-backed vinyl | Softer, less hollow |
| Kitchen in a dry house | Either | Water-resistant laminate or 20 mil vinyl |

### Using both

Many homes run laminate in living spaces and bedrooms and vinyl in wet rooms, joined with a T-molding. Paint ceilings before the new floor goes down; our [ceiling paint guide](/best-ceiling-paint/) covers the low-spatter options.

### Care that keeps either floor looking new

Sweep or vacuum on a hard-floor setting and use a barely damp microfiber mop with an approved cleaner. Never wet-mop or steam-mop laminate. Keep felt pads on furniture, a mat under rolling chairs and a spare carton for repairs. Holding indoor humidity around 35 to 55 percent keeps laminate movement within what the joints can absorb.

mistakes.title: Putting a budget AC3 board in the kitchen
mistakes.body: Entry-level laminate is fine in bedrooms, but kitchens, entries and pet-heavy rooms wear through it much faster. Pay the small premium for an AC4, water-resistant board in those spaces, and keep the cheaper line for rooms that mostly see socks and slippers.

mistakes.title: Trapping the floor at the edges
mistakes.body: Laminate expands and contracts with humidity. A missing gap at walls, jambs or cabinets, or trim nailed into the boards, pins the floor so it buckles or opens at the joints. Keep the full gap, undercut door casings and nail trim only to the wall.

mistakes.title: Skipping the vapor barrier on concrete
mistakes.body: A slab releases moisture constantly, even when it looks dry. Without a 6 mil poly barrier or a combination pad, that vapor works into the fiberboard core and swells the board edges. Test the slab, lay the barrier with taped seams and run it slightly up the wall.

mistakes.title: Cleaning with a wet mop or steam
mistakes.body: The core is wood fiber. Water driven into the joints by a soaked mop or steam mop swells the edges over time, even on water-resistant lines. Use a barely damp microfiber pad and a cleaner the manufacturer approves, and wipe spills dry the same day.

mistakes.title: Doubling up on underlayment
mistakes.body: Boards with an attached pad are engineered to sit directly on the subfloor or a thin poly barrier. Adding a foam pad beneath them makes the floor too soft, so the joints flex and break. Read the carton: if a pad is attached, add only a vapor barrier on slabs.

faqs.q: What is the best laminate flooring brand?
faqs.a: Pergo is the best all-round laminate brand for most homes, and Pergo Outlast+ balances spill protection, scratch resistance and availability. Mohawk RevWood Plus is the pick for heavy spill exposure, Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus for realism, Shaw Repel and Mannington Restoration for thick, solid boards, and AquaGuard or TrafficMaster for value.

faqs.q: What is the best quality laminate flooring?
faqs.a: The best quality laminate for a typical home is an AC4, water-resistant board in the 8 to 12 mm range with sealed edges and a strong locking joint. Mannington Restoration and Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus sit at the premium end for realism and thickness, while Pergo Outlast+ and Mohawk RevWood Plus deliver top performance at mainstream cost.

faqs.q: Do I need AC4 or is AC3 enough?
faqs.a: AC3 handles bedrooms, guest rooms and living spaces with modest traffic. Choose AC4 for kitchens, hallways, entries and homes with active kids or large dogs. The cost difference is usually small, and the harder surface is the cheapest way to extend the life of a busy floor. AC5 is commercial grade.

faqs.q: What is the best scratch proof laminate flooring?
faqs.a: No laminate is truly scratch proof, but an AC4-rated board with a low-gloss or matte finish resists and hides scratches best. Pergo Outlast+, Mohawk RevWood Plus and Shaw Repel all carry hard surfaces suited to pets. Mats at doors, felt pads and trimmed pet nails matter as much as the rating.

faqs.q: Can laminate flooring go on a concrete floor?
faqs.a: Yes. Test the slab for moisture first, fill dips to meet the flatness tolerance, then lay a 6 mil poly vapor barrier or a combination pad with taped seams before floating the laminate. A water-resistant AC4 line is the best choice. If the slab shows active moisture, fix the source or choose vinyl plank.

faqs.q: Can laminate survive a spill or leak?
faqs.a: Modern water-resistant laminate tolerates topical spills for a warranted window, often 24 to 72 hours depending on the line. It will not survive a flood, an unnoticed plumbing leak or water rising from a slab, and warranties exclude those. Wipe spills promptly and use vinyl plank in full baths and laundry rooms.

faqs.q: Is laminate or vinyl plank better?
faqs.a: Laminate is better for scratch resistance, realism and a wood-like feel in dry rooms such as living rooms, bedrooms and hallways. Vinyl plank is better wherever water can sit or rise from below, including full baths, laundry rooms and basements, because its core cannot swell. Many homes use both, split by room.

bottomLine: Pergo Outlast+ is the best laminate flooring for most homes, combining spill protection, a hard surface and easy availability. Step up to Mohawk RevWood Plus if spills are constant, choose Quick-Step NatureTEK Plus or Mannington Restoration for realism and thickness, Shaw Repel for a solid feel underfoot, AquaGuard for whole-house value and TrafficMaster for low-traffic bedrooms and rentals. Whatever brand you pick, match the AC rating to the room, keep the perimeter gap generous, lay a vapor barrier on concrete and keep water off the core. Where a room has a tub, a washer or a damp slab, pair your laminate with vinyl plank instead.
